qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Local depot density and route logistics provide modest distribution scale, but post-tax GAAP ROIC is sub-hurdle at ~8-10% (well below the 12% Munger threshold) with razor-thin operating margins (~3-4%). As a bulk fuel/LPG distributor, pricing power is limited to a thin delivery markup over volatile commodity costs.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3 (Rejected – G3 Moat & Pricing). While heating fuel and LPG delivery fulfill an essential physical need, DCC operates as a high-volume, low-margin distributor with thin ~3-4% operating margins and a multi-year post-tax ROIC below the 12% hurdle (~8-10%). It lacks independent pricing power against commodity swings and faces long-term structural volume headwinds from European building decarbonization and the energy transition.
qualitative.evidence: International energy distribution and services group with over £14B continuing revenue (transitioning to pure-play DCC Energy after divesting Healthcare and Technology). Historical ROCE/ROIC hovers around 8-11% post-tax. Although cash conversion is consistently high (>90-100%), the business is constrained by commodity price pass-through dynamics and thin ~3.5% adjusted operating margins.
